sources: Matthew 20:1-2 (a landowner goes out early to hire laborers for his vineyard, agreeing to a denarius a day)
Matthew 20:3-5 (he goes out again about the third, sixth and ninth hour)
Matthew 20:6-7 (about the eleventh hour: “Why do you stand here all day idle?” “Because no one has hired us.” “You also go into the vineyard”)
Matthew 20:8-10 (paid from the last to the first; each receives a denarius; the first thought they would receive more)
Matthew 20:11-12 (“These last have spent one hour, and you have made them equal to us, who have borne the burden of the day and the scorching heat!”)
Matthew 20:13, 15 (“Friend, I am doing you no wrong. Didn’t you agree with me for a denarius?… Or is your eye evil, because I am good?”)
Matthew 20:16 (“So the last will be first, and the first last”)
Captions follow the World English Bible, lightly modernized; “are you envious because I am good?” follows common modern renderings of 20:15

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? have you ever watched someone get something you worked much harder for?
options: that’s honest. this story knows that feeling.
then you’ll know the joy in this story too.
good. keep this one for the day it happens.

steps.line: A landowner went out at dawn to hire workers for his vineyard. He agreed to pay them a denarius, the usual day’s wage.
steps.label: Matthew 20:1-2

steps.line: He went back at nine, at noon, and at three, and hired more.
steps.label: Matthew 20:3-5

steps.line: At five, an hour before quitting time, he found others still standing around. “No one has hired us.” “You go into the vineyard too.”
steps.label: Matthew 20:6-7

steps.q: At evening, the last ones hired, who worked one hour, are paid first. What do you guess they get?
o: One hour’s pay, fair and square
steps.why: A full day’s pay, for one hour. A denarius was the usual day’s wage; many scholars say it was about what a family needed to eat for a day.

steps.line: The ones who came at five got a full day’s pay. The ones hired at dawn were sure they’d get more.
steps.label: Matthew 20:8-10

steps.line: They got the same, and grumbled: “These last worked one hour, and you made them equal to us, who bore the heat of the day!”
steps.label: Matthew 20:11-12

steps.q: You worked from dawn, in the heat. You get exactly what you agreed. Were you cheated?
o: No: you got the full, fair wage
Yes: equal pay for unequal work
Yes: you should have been paid first
steps.why: The landowner keeps his word to the letter. Nobody gets less than fair; some get more than fair. The sting is in the comparing.

steps.line: “Friend, I’m doing you no wrong. Didn’t you agree to a denarius? Or are you envious because I am good?”
steps.label: Matthew 20:13, 15

steps.q: The landowner pays everyone that same evening. Why would Jesus’s listeners expect that?
o: The Torah says pay a day worker by sunset
Coins weren’t safe to keep overnight
Workers would quit if not paid daily
steps.why: Deuteronomy says pay a poor worker the same day, “for he is poor and his heart is set on it.” A day without work meant a night without food.

steps.q: In the Greek, the landowner literally asks: “Is your eye evil because I am good?” What did an “evil eye” mean then?
o: A curse you could put on someone
A sign that you were lying
steps.why: In Jewish speech of the time, a “bad eye” meant stinginess or envy, and a “good eye” meant generosity. Jesus sets them side by side.

say: here’s what i love. the landowner keeps going back to the market, all day long, looking for anyone still standing there.
christians read it as a picture of grace: God’s love isn’t a wage you earn by the hour. whether someone comes at dawn or at the last hour, the welcome is whole.

steps.q: The grumblers are the ones who worked all day. What might Jesus be gently warning people who’ve been faithful for years?
o: That long service earns a bigger reward
That latecomers must make up the time
Not to resent God’s gift to latecomers
steps.why: Long faithfulness is good, but it can turn into scorekeeping. Jesus ends: “So the last will be first, and the first last.”

today.say: generosity isn’t fair. it’s better. today, when someone gets something you think they didn’t earn, a break, a second chance, a win, choose to be glad for them, and tell them so.
options: then tell them today. that’s the landowner’s joy, shared.
it’s hard for most of us. that’s why jesus told it. start with one.
